# Results — Study 780 (Long-Weekend-Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **SPY
drifts up on the pre-holiday session** (the classic pre-holiday effect: the last trading day
before a market holiday earns an abnormally positive return). Single-series & self-benchmarked
— "abnormal" means excess over SPY's own mean daily return. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `120ff40dea08` (SPY adjusted/total-return daily
closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `SPY` (S&P 500 ETF): 5,555 rows, 2004-06-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 192 NYSE full-day closures 2005→2025, real dates from the NYSE holiday schedule (Juneteenth from 2022); the traded *session* is the last SPY close strictly before each holiday, resolved from the tape |
| Events resolvable | all **192** of 192 holidays have SPY coverage around the eve session |
| Baseline | SPY mean ordinary-day return **+0.0484%/day** — the "normal day" the pre-holiday excess is measured against |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the excess return across independent, non-overlapping holiday events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife; an old/recent sub-sample split |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: the NYSE schedule is published years ahead. eve = last close before the holiday; run-up = [eve−3 → eve]; net of 2× one-way cost. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) |

## The pre-holiday drift — excess return over an ordinary SPY day

| cut | n | mean excess | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| holiday-eve (pre1) | 192 | +0.0964% | +1.532 | 112/192 = 58.3% [51.3%, 65.1%] |
| 3-session run-up (pre3) | 192 | **+0.2986%** | **+2.195** | 113/192 = 58.9% [51.8%, 65.6%] |

The direction the folklore predicts is **there** — the holiday-eve session beats an ordinary
day by ~0.10%, and the broader 3-session run-up by ~0.30% — and the hit rate clears 50% on
both cuts (Wilson lower bound > 51%). But the **classic single-eve cut is not significant**
(*t* = +1.53). The effect only crosses the line when you widen to the 3-session run-up
(*t* = +2.20). Positive and real-directional, but weak and window-dependent.

## The post-holiday session (reversal check)

| cut | n | mean excess | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| post-holiday (post1) | 192 | −0.0314% | −0.384 | 90/192 = 46.9% [39.9%, 53.9%] |

The first session *after* the holiday is a **clean zero** (*t* = −0.38): there is a faint
give-back but nothing tradable, so the eve drift is not simply borrowed from the day after.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| eve (pre1) | right | +0.0964% | −0.0005% (0.0850%) | 0.1263 |
| run-up (pre3) | right | +0.2986% | −0.0022% (0.1376%) | **0.0145** |

The single-eve drift sits only ~1.1σ into the right tail (p = 0.13 — inside the luck cloud).
The **3-session run-up is genuinely in the tail** (p = 0.0145): only ~1.5% of random 3-day
SPY windows drifted this much. So the run-up is *not* ordinary noise — but the classic
one-day version is.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — holiday-eve (pre1) *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+1.532**; across all 192 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[+1.273, +1.815]** — the (weak, positive) tilt is broad, not one holiday, but it never
reaches significance under any single deletion.

## Did the anomaly decay? (pre1, old vs recent halves)

| sub-sample | n | mean excess | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| first half (2005→2015) | 96 | +0.0718% | +0.701 |
| second half (2015→2025) | 96 | +0.1210% | +1.644 |

Unlike the textbook story — where calendar anomalies fade *after* publication — the eve drift
is, if anything, mildly *stronger* in the recent half, but both halves are individually
insignificant. No decay, no confirmation; just persistent weakness.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| holiday-eve | +0.0964% (*t* +1.53) | −0.0036% (*t* −0.06) | −0.1036% (*t* −1.65) |
| 3-session run-up | +0.2986% (*t* +2.20) | +0.1986% (*t* +1.46) | +0.0986% (*t* +0.72) |

The **single-day eve trade is entirely eaten by costs** — net of a 5 bps one-way round-trip
it is exactly zero (*t* −0.06) and goes negative at 10 bps. The 3-session run-up keeps a
positive net edge at 5 bps (+0.20%) but the *t* falls below 1.5 and it is gone by 10 bps.
SPY capacity is ample, so this is a *cost/robustness* fragility, not a size one.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.06 (sd 1.05); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  at n ≈ 190 events the one-sample *t* is well-behaved (~5% false-positive rate, unlike a
  small-n design), so a *t* = 1.53 really is unremarkable.
- **Planted eve bump +0.2%:** mean excess +0.161%, *t* = **+1.97**.
- **Planted eve bump +0.4%:** mean excess +0.354%, *t* = **+4.34** — a real bump is recovered
  monotonically, and the detector is easily powered to see one this size at this n.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The pre-holiday drift is *directionally real and jackknife-stable* — the eve beats an ordinary day (+0.10%, hit 58%) and the 3-session run-up clears the placebo (+0.30%, *t* = +2.20, right-tail p = 0.014). But the **classic single-eve cut is insignificant** (*t* = +1.53, p = 0.13), the effect only reaches significance on the wider window, and the detector is well-powered at n = 190 — so this is a genuine-but-weak tilt, not a *t* ≥ 2.5 result. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Fragile** | Survives *gross* on the run-up (*t* = 2.2) with ample SPY capacity, but the single-day version is **zeroed by a 5 bps round-trip** and the run-up's net edge (+0.20% @ 5 bps, *t* = 1.46) is marginal and vanishes by 10 bps. A break-even-ish, cost-sensitive curiosity, not a bankable edge. |

**In one sentence:** the famous pre-holiday drift is *faintly present in the right direction*
— the 3-session run-up into a holiday beats the tape (+0.30%, placebo p = 0.014) — but the
textbook single-eve version is statistically unremarkable (*t* = 1.53) and dies the moment
you pay a spread, leaving a weak, cost-fragile echo of the old anomaly rather than a tradable
edge.
